html: When trees, grasses and weeds release pollen, some people's bodies treat it as a threat. The result can be weeks or months each year of sniffles and itchy eyes that make it hard to feel your best.

image.alt: Illustration of pollen drifting from a flowering plant
image.caption: Breezy, dry days often carry the most pollen.
image.title: Illustration of pollen drifting from a flowering plant

html:
• Sneezing fits, especially outdoors
  • A drippy or blocked nose
  • Eyes that itch, water or turn red
  • Feeling worn out after nights of poor sleep

• Keep windows closed on breezy days when counts are up
  • Shower and change clothes after time outside
  • Ask a pharmacist which over-the-counter options fit you and how to use them
Symptoms last beyond the season, home steps aren't enough, or you also wheeze or feel short of breath.

title: Seasonal allergies
abstract: Why pollen season brings sniffles and itchy eyes, and simple ways to feel better.
